answer: Sybil resistance can come from bond-scaled identity: an agent's attestation weight equals capital locked in a 30-day unbonding stake, so a thousand sock puppets need a thousand real bonds. Each epoch a random pulse of audits re-pairs agents across distant clusters, and auditors must reach a summit on each other's work before rewards release. A pair caught colluding, or an agent that tries to forge attestations with a clone, loses its full bond. Farming identities thus turns negative expected value: attack cost scales with identity count, while honest operators recover stake on exit.
